status: prospective follow-up; previous scan suggested same-reader/opposing-writer pairs but did not test this hypothesis
hypothesis: Some native units implement a difference between two nonlinear conditions through a common signed output direction, rather than a linear channel or duplicate unit.
identity: For gi=g(zi), gj=g(zj), w=(wi-wj)/2 and r=(wi+wj)/2, the native pair output is exactly w*(gi-gj)+r*(gi+gj) in real arithmetic. This algebra holds for every pair and alone proves no learned structure.
candidate: Retain both original affine readers and both native GELUs. Compare dropping the common term r*(gi+gj) with dropping the contrast term w*(gi-gj), dropping individual units, and dropping the whole pair.
proposal_bank: Reuse all64positive-reader geometry pairs perlayer from the frozen native_gelu_relations scan. All4layers. No new pair selection using validation responses.
measurements: Actual contrast and common term magnitudes on all4096training and1024fit-disjoint evaluation parent states.
Full pair-replacement error relative to pair removal and native MLP output RMS.

interpretation: A small r weight does not imply its computation is negligible: close gi,gj can suppress the contrast term and amplify the relative importance of the common term.
A compact signed writer relation must beat a simple-removal explanation, preserve actual finite edits, and survive autonomous full-model KL before acceptance.
Readability of selected text contexts does not establish a mechanism; semantic labels remain hypotheses.
